items.title: Nowhere to hide: Tech selloff hits software and chip stocks alike
items.description: The software and semiconductor sectors haven’t been trading in tandem much this year, but they collectively fell Friday as AI and interest-rate fears hit the market.

items.title: This Senate race where data centers are a crucial issue has more spending than any other midterm clash
items.description: Money is pouring in and funding intense, negative ads: “It’s everywhere, and you can’t escape it.”

items.title: Could an Anthropic IPO put your 401(k) at risk? The AI safety debate hits a new dimension.
items.description: Anthropic and New York City’s comptroller have opened a line of communication to discuss “existential risks” posed by AI and what that could mean for the company’s future stock.

items.title: The bond market shrugged off two inflation shocks. Why stock investors should pay attention.
items.description: Hot CPI and PPI data should have pushed Treasury yields higher. Instead, bond buyers stepped in to suggest yields have risen high enough to become attractive for investors.

items.title: New SEC rules would fleece everyday investors to enrich Wall Street
items.description: New proposals from the Securities and Exchange Commission will tilt the scales in favor of Wall Street and against a huge group of retail investors.

items.title: I’m 63 and diagnosed with lymphoma. Should I take my Social Security next year?
items.description: “My plan is to continue working as long as I’m able to do so and invest my Social Security benefits while I’m still earning a paycheck.”

items.title: Don’t buy this dip: Several signs suggest there’s more pain ahead for tech stocks
items.description: Thinking of buying the dip in technology stocks? The Nasdaq Composite’s technical outlook suggests don’t do it — at least not yet.

items.title: EchoStar’s stock looks like a stealthy way to ride the SpaceX wave, J.P. Morgan says
items.description: Investors aren’t giving EchoStar enough credit for the value of its future SpaceX stake or its potential to strike more spectrum deals, an analyst argues.

items.title: Are we spending our retirement money in the right order? Our plan is: Social Security, annuities, cash — then IRA.
items.description: Spending all your cash first can make your income surge in later years.

items.title: Your Social Security check will rise an average of $75 a month — will it be able to keep up with inflation?
